guia.what: A flex layout with semantic spacing—direction (`flex-col`, `flex-row`), `gap-*`, alignment, and wrap, all with `ts` utilities. Grid’s sibling.
whenUse: The elements run in a single direction, like a column of sections or a row of buttons.
What matters is the space between items, not aligning them into columns.
You want the same spacing rhythm as the rest of the system.
whenAvoid: The elements need to line up in rows and columns → `grid`.
It’s the width of the whole page → `container`.
dos: Use the system’s gaps instead of one-off margins on the children.
If the block is a region, use the right semantic element.
donts: Don’t add margins to the children to fix the spacing. Change the `gap`.
Don’t force a grid out of nested stacks → `grid`.
